Delta-only review. The R1 cost qualifications in governed f5f327f remain:64 updates/128 canonical retirement facts per ACTUAL sweep, not all candidate work, bytes, notices, launches or a64/minute bound; the debug copy timing is not a full-sweep/CPU benchmark. Policy remains the tombstoned recipient; age, revive exclusion, successful reads/re-read and LIMIT remain BRAKES. This cost verdict does not replace the independent reviewer's destructive-ordering verdict.

B332-01 fix adds one Option<ReviveIntent> field to each SpawnHold (None on ordinary holds). carry moves the existing intent into that field; it adds no heap allocation, map entry, scan, schema/queue call, timer, polling loop, process launch or spawn site. Per hold/revive storage and handoff work are O(1), plus the EXISTING intent's owned seat string. The existing map insert/count/decrement/removal occurs once per intent; only its owner/lifetime changes. The existing sweep's revives() still clones active distinct keys O(R): a cancelled-but-running revive now remains in R until its launch finishes, correctly extending the brake. O(1) field size is not an O(1) sweep or a bounded launch lifetime.

The intent is taken before pane/lock waits as before. carry follows lock acquisition without an intervening await. The unchanged launch_seat_locked moves SpawnHold into the existing owned task; launch_owned drops it immediately after put_lifting_owner_close succeeds and retains it through its existing rollback/failure paths. Normal return and panic drop the owned Option. No new task, timeout or retry mechanism is introduced; a stalled launch can retain its existing protection until completion. Stop still waits on the existing launch lock; hard exit or a stop past its existing bound can lose the in-memory brake, as disclosed. These constraints are not new resource ceilings.
